meta.title: Thai B2 Upper Intermediate
meta.subtitle: 1500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Thai → English (see the Thai, recall the meaning) and English → Thai (see an English meaning, recall the Thai). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1500 words for an upper-intermediate learner, aligned to B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand the main ideas of complex text on both concrete and abstract topics, including technical discussions in their field of specialisation' — a learner here is able to interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction with native speakers quite possible without strain for either party, and to produce clear, detailed text on a wide range of subjects and explain a viewpoint on a topical issue, giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Thai, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 346 of the 1500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — politics and public administration, the law and the courts, the economy, business and finance, science and research, technology and the internet, the environment and natural resources, health, medicine and the mind, the arts, literature and the media, history and society, Buddhism and Thai institutions, argument and evaluation — the words for claims, evidence, causes and consequences — the formal connectors of written Thai, and the verbs of reporting, analysing and persuading — and the other 1154 are the commonest remaining words of Thai, taken from the word counts of the Thai National Corpus, a large collection of written Thai. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword is printed in Thai script with a romanisation beneath it in the Paiboon system, which marks the TONE on every syllable — no mark for mid, à low, â falling, á high, ǎ rising — because a Thai word said on the wrong tone is a different word; the Thai Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script and the rules that decide a tone. 136 nouns show the classifier they are counted with (a house is counted in หลัง, an animal in ตัว), and there are no forms to learn: Thai words never change shape. Example sentences come with 492 of the 1500 words, three apiece for 175 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, romanisation, classifiers and some example sentences: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: the Thai National Corpus word list as distributed by PyThaiNLP (CC0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
